items.slide_topic: Param history: LeNet-5 (1998), about 60,000 trainable parameters
items.dek: The network in figure 2 contains 340,908 connections, but only 60,000 trainable free parameters because of the weight sharing.
items.outlet: Proceedings of the IEEE (LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, Haffner: Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition)
items.caption: LeNet-5 (1998): 60,000 trainable free parameters
items.notes: Sentence from the loaded PDF text layer; pdftotext dropped the 'fi' ligature (printed 'gure'), restored here. This copy says 340,908 connections; Epoch's note quotes 390408 connections. The 60,000 figure matches in both. The yann.lecun.com copy (also downloaded) had no extractable copy of this sentence, so the Stanford-hosted copy is the cited source. Date is Epoch's publication date.

items.dek: The neural network, which has 60 million parameters and 650,000 neurons, consists of five convolutional layers, some of which are followed by max-pooling layers,
items.outlet: NeurIPS 2012 (Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton: ImageNet Classification with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks)
items.caption: AlexNet (2012): 60 million parameters
items.notes: Abstract sentence from the loaded PDF (text cut at the end of the line; the sentence continues). The same paper also states 'Our neural network architecture has 60 million parameters.' A WebFetch summary of the NeurIPS abstract page said '500,000 neurons'; the PDF says 650,000 - use 650,000. Date is Epoch's publication date (2012-09-30).

items.dek: Our largest model, GPT-2, is a 1.5B parameter Transformer that achieves state of the art results on 7 out of 8 tested language modeling datasets in a zero-shot setting but still underfits WebText.
items.outlet: OpenAI (Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners)
items.caption: GPT-2 (2019): 1.5 billion parameters
items.notes: Abstract from the loaded PDF. Table 2 of the same paper lists the largest model as 1542M parameters with 48 layers and width 1600; 1.5B is the headline (rounded) figure. The OpenAI blog post openai.com/index/better-language-models/ returned HTTP 403 and was not loaded. Epoch labels its GPT-2 (1.5B) record 'Speculative' even though the paper states the figure.

items.dek: Specifically, we train GPT-3, an autoregressive language model with 175 billion parameters, 10x more than any previous non-sparse language model
items.outlet: arXiv (Brown et al.: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners)
items.caption: GPT-3 (2020): 175 billion parameters
items.notes: Sentence from the loaded arXiv PDF (introduction). The arXiv abstract page https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.14165 was also loaded: submitted 28 May 2020 (v1). Appendix Table D.1 lists GPT-3 175B at 174,600 (millions), i.e. 174.6B; main-text Table 2.1 lists 175.0B.

items.dek: we pre-trained a flagship model with 405B trainable parameters on 15.6T text tokens.
items.outlet: Meta AI (The Llama 3 Herd of Models)
items.caption: Llama 3.1 405B (2024): 405B trainable parameters
items.notes: Sentence from the loaded arXiv PDF (introduction). Epoch's record for Llama 3.1-405B is dated 2024-07-23 and labelled Confident.

items.dek: DeepSeek-V3 comprises 671B total parameters, of which 37B are activated for each token.
items.caption: DeepSeek-V3 (2024): 671B total parameters, 37B active per token
items.notes: Sentence from the loaded arXiv PDF. Mixture-of-experts model: the total is far larger than the per-token active count. Date is Epoch's date for DeepSeek-V3.

items.slide_topic: Param history: Llama 4 (2025), active vs total parameters
items.dek: Llama 4 Behemoth, a 288 billion active parameter model with 16 experts that is our most powerful yet and among the world’s smartest LLMs.
items.caption: Llama 4 Behemoth (2025 preview): 288B active parameters; no total stated in this post
items.notes: Sentence from the loaded Meta blog text. The same post says 'Llama 4 Maverick models have 17B active parameters and 400B total parameters.' Meta does not state Behemoth's total in this post. Epoch's 2e12 total for Behemoth is Epoch's own estimate (label Likely = within 10x); do not show 2T as a Meta figure.

items.notes: Quote is from the loaded ForkLog article, which embeds Alibaba Group's X post. The Alibaba post and the qwen.ai blog were not loaded (qwen.ai returned no text). Epoch lists 'Qwen 3.8 Max' at 2.4e12 (Confident, dated 2026-07-19) and 'Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B' (2026-08-08). The ~95B active figure comes from Epoch's note and press, not a primary source here.

items.slide_topic: Param history: Grok 4.7 (2026), 2.1 trillion per press
items.headline: xAI Launches Grok 4.7. It's Bigger, But Late to the AI Frontier Party
items.dek: Grok 4.7 packs 2.1 trillion parameters, up 40% from the 1.5 trillion in Grok 4.6
items.caption: Grok 4.7 (Sep 2026): 2.1 trillion parameters, as reported by Decrypt
items.notes: Sentence from the loaded Decrypt article (headline and date also from the page). The article states the figure without a technical source, and no xAI technical document turned up in search. Epoch's notable CSV row for Grok 4.7 holds 2100000000.0 (2.1e9), which contradicts that row's own note ('the 2.1T model'); treated as a units error, so the press figure is used in the chart.

IEEE, Stanford-hosted copy); Krizhevsky et al. 2012 (NeurIPS PDF); OpenAI 2019 GPT-2 paper (Table 2: 1542M); Brown et al. 2020 GPT-3 (text; Table D.1: 174,600M). datasets.title: Total parameters of frontier-class models, 2024-2026 (published figures, Epoch estimates, press)
datasets.unit: parameters (total, not active); log10 axis recommended
labels: Llama 4 Behemoth (Apr 2025, Epoch estimate; Meta gives 288B active only)
datasets.source: Epoch AI notable_ai_models.csv (Oct 8, 2026) for dates and Epoch labels; published totals from the primary pages in items[]. Epoch labels: Confident = within 3x, Likely = within 10x, Speculative = within 30x. Excluded: Kimi K3 (Epoch 2.8e12, Speculative; no primary source). Grok 4.7 Epoch CSV value (2.1e9) is a units error against its own note; press figure used. Closed models GPT-4o, GPT-4.5, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-6 Astra have no Epoch parameter estimate. Full extract: neural-nets-param-history-epoch-extract.csv.

facts.claim: From LeNet-5 (60,000) to GPT-3 (175 billion) is about 2.9 million times more parameters, over 22 years (1998 to 2020). Computed by us from the two papers' figures.
From AlexNet (60 million) to GPT-3 (175 billion) is about 2,900 times more parameters, over 8 years (2012 to 2020). Computed by us from the two papers' figures.
Llama 3.1 405B: 'we pre-trained a flagship model with 405B trainable parameters on 15.6T text tokens.'
facts.source: Meta AI, The Llama 3 Herd of Models (arXiv 2407.21783)

facts.claim: DeepSeek-V3 (Dec 2024) has 671B total parameters, of which 37B are activated for each token.
Meta's Llama 4 Behemoth preview post gives 288 billion active parameters and does not state a total; Llama 4 Maverick is 17B active and 400B total.
Kimi K2 (Jul 2025): 1 trillion total parameters, 32 billion activated.
facts.source: Moonshot AI, Kimi K2 project page

facts.claim: Kimi K2.5 (Feb 2026): 'The model comprises 1.04 trillion total parameters with 32 billion activated'.
